# Native CLI file-access review

The simulator and headless runner are local applications using the invoking user's filesystem permissions. `--experiment FILE`, `--compare FILE`, and `--output FILE` intentionally select local files. These paths are not accepted by a network service and the executables do not establish an elevated-privilege file-access boundary.

CodeQL `cpp/path-injection` findings follow these explicit CLI selections into their file operations (`--experiment`, `--compare` and `--output` through the shared reader and CSV writer). Alert numbers change whenever the code moves, so triage by rule and contract, not by number. They are false positives for privilege escalation under this contract. Preserve user-selected file access; reassess the findings if these operations become a privileged service or consume paths automatically from remote inputs. No query-wide suppression is used.

Native CSV creation uses an explicit owner-read/write mode on POSIX instead of inheriting permissive creation permissions from `fopen`. The browser export continues using its temporary virtual-filesystem stream. CLI tests verify creation under umask zero and preservation of an existing file's mode.

CSV output targets (2026-10-06, A57). `solar-lab --output` checks the destination with `lstat` and accepts only a missing path or an existing regular file: symlinks (including dangling ones), FIFOs, devices and directories are refused, so a link target is never truncated and a FIFO never blocks the run. Output is written to a `mkstemp` temporary beside the destination (created 0600 with `O_EXCL`), given the existing file's permission bits when one is being replaced, flushed and `fsync`ed, then `rename`d into place only after the whole series succeeds. Any failure deletes the temporary, leaving the previous file intact or no file at all. The replacement is a new inode: ownership and hard links of the old file are not carried over, and a destination swapped for a symlink between the check and the rename has only its directory entry replaced, never its target written. Native `E` snapshots use exclusive creation of the next free `solar-snapshot-NNN.csv` and never replace an existing file. Windows builds keep in-place writes.

Round-2 follow-ups (2026-10-06). Because `rename` needs write permission on the directory rather than the file, an existing read-only destination is refused up front with `access(W_OK)` (EACCES), matching the earlier `O_TRUNC` behaviour; root may still replace it, as root could truncate it before. Conversely, a writable file inside a non-writable directory now fails, since the temporary cannot be created beside it; `--help` states both rules. Empty `--output` values and names ending in `/` are usage errors before any work. SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP delete the temporary through an async-signal-safe handler (a fixed path buffer published by a `sig_atomic_t` flag, `unlink`, then the default action is restored and the signal re-raised); signals the parent shell ignored stay ignored. After `rename` the containing directory is `fsync`ed on a best-effort basis. Native `E` reports the failure reason, including when all 999 numbered names are taken. CLI tests cover symlink, dangling symlink, FIFO and failure cleanup under a file-size limit.

Catalog import names are bounded by the parser and copied into session-owned buffers through a size-aware operation. Tests cover the maximum accepted name, rejected overlong input, ownership across reset, and preservation of the prior session on rejection.

Vendored decoder (2026-10-07, A65). `src/render/third_party/stb_image.h` (pinned stb_image v2.30, see its README) is compiled into `build/src/render/image_decode.o` before `codeql init`, so CodeQL's traced build reuses that object and does not analyze third-party code; `paths-ignore` is ignored for manually built C/C++. The decoder only ever reads the project's own pinned textures, decodes from memory with JPEG/PNG compiled in, and refuses images over 8192 px per edge before allocating (`render_decode_image`). Our wrapper and every first-party file remain analyzed.
